issue.title: Visiting different subdomains in different specs throws error

repository.name: cypress
repository.description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

issue.body:
<!--
Thanks for opening an issue!

- Your best chance of getting a bug looked at quickly is to provide a repository with a reproducible bug that can be cloned and run.
- If you need general advice, join our chat: https://gitter.im/cypress-io/cypress
-->

* Operating System: OS X 10.11.6
* Cypress Version: 0.19.1

### Are you requesting a feature or reporting a bug?
🐛 

### Current behavior:
If `baseUrl` has not been set in `cypress.json` or `baseUrl` is set  to the same url as `firstBaseUrl` below, then the first inner describe block runs, and the second throws a Security Error.

If `baseUrl` is set in `cypress.json` to another url of the same superdomain, then neither inner describe block runs.

Everything runs beautifully if I set `chromeWebSecurity` to false in `cypress.json`

### Expected behavior:
No security errors should be thrown when visiting different subdomains of the same site in different specs. (I think the high ideal might be that visiting entirely different superdomains in different specs won't error out).

### How to reproduce the current behavior:
See above.

#### Test code:
Here's our current setup:
cypress.env.json
```json
{
  "firstBaseUrl": "https://first-app.herokuapp.com",
  "secondBaseUrl": "https://second-app.herokuapp.com"
}
```

open_enrollment_class_flow_spec.js
```js
describe('Open enrollment class flow', function(){
  var firstUrl = Cypress.env('firstBaseUrl')
  var secondUrl = Cypress.env('secondBaseUrl')

  describe('First App', function(){
    beforeEach(function(){
      cy.visit(`${firstUrl}/sessions/new`)
    })

    it('should be able to foo', function(){
      cy.firstAppLogin()
        .visit(`${firstUrl}/open_enrollment_classes/new`)
        // do DOM stuff
        })
    })
  })

  describe('second App', function(){
    it('should have a new bar', function(){
      cy.visit(`${secondUrl}/users/sign_in`)
        .secondAppLogin()
        // do DOM stuff
    })
  })
```

### Additional Info (images, notes, stack traces, etc)
General goal (for context): integration testing microservices

issue.title: Unable to successfully request any website within Cypress browser

repository.name: cypress
repository.description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

issue.body:
<!-- **Tip** in order for us to reproduce the bug you can fork [cypress-io/cypress-test-tiny](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-test-tiny) repo and setup the failing test. Then just tells us the repo and branch to try! -->

- Operating System: Windows 7
- Cypress Version: 1.4.1
- Browser Version: Chrome 60.0.3112.78

### Is this a Feature or Bug?
Bug

### Current behavior:
When making a cy.request() to localhost within the Cypress browser, the request consistently fails (404). Copying and pasting the localhost address directly in a new tab within the Cypress browser causes a redirect to a new IP which will also fail (500), with an ESOCKETTIMEDOUT error. This behavior only occurs within the Cypress browser, whereas localhost returns a successful response when inside of a normal Chrome browser window.

After reviewing similar issues, and inspecting the proxy settings for both the Cypress browser and the Chrome browser, there is a difference observed between the two.

### Desired behavior:
Making a cy.request() to localhost should return a successful response, if a successful request can be observed outside of the Cypress test suite.

### How to reproduce:

1. Note that making cy.request() of localhost in Cypress browser results in failure
2. Note that navigating directly to localhost in Cypress browser results in failure
3. Note that navigating directly to localhost in Chrome browser results in success

issue.title: Allow .localhost tld to be parsed correctly

repository.name: cypress
repository.description: Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

issue.body:
Closes #451

Currently `parseDomain` returns an invalid response when passed a domain ending in `.localhost`. For example, `www.ourapp.localhost` returns:
```
domain: "loc"
subdomain: "www.ourapp"
tld: "local"
```

This PR adds `.localhost` to the `customTlds` list so that the domain is parsed correctly:
```
domain: "ourapp"
subdomain: "www"
tld: "localhost"
```

This PR closes #451
